what_its_for: Polatuzumab vedotin is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a type of blood cancer called diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that has come back or has not responded to previous treatments. It works by targeting and killing cancer cells directly, helping to slow or stop the growth of the cancer.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (a slow injection into your vein) by a nurse or doctor in a clinic or hospital setting. You will NOT give yourself this medication at home. Each infusion typically takes about 90 minutes for your first dose. If you tolerated it well, later infusions may take about 30 minutes. You will be watched closely during and after each infusion for any reactions.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body weight. It is usually given once every 21 days (one cycle = 3 weeks) for a total of 6 cycles. Before each infusion, you will likely receive medicines to help prevent allergic reactions and nausea. Never change your dose or schedule on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given to you by a healthcare team, it is unlikely you will miss a dose on your own. However, if you need to cancel or miss a scheduled appointment, call your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule. It is very important to stay on track with your treatment schedule to get the best results.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home. It is prepared and stored by the hospital or clinic. If you are given any take-home medicines that go along with your treatment, store them exactly as directed on their labels and keep them out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid being around people who are sick or have infections, since this medicine can weaken your immune system and make it harder to fight germs. Avoid live vaccines (such as the flu nasal spray or shingles vaccine) during treatment — ask your doctor before getting any vaccinations. Avoid drinking alcohol or taking new medicines, vitamins, or supplements without checking with your doctor first. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should not use this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Men should also use birth control during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while receiving this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: fever (temperature above 100.4°F or 38°C), chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hands or feet; severe tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath or chest pain; severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; confusion or difficulty thinking clearly; swelling in your legs or ankles; any infusion reactions such as rash, itching, flushing, dizziness, or difficulty breathing during or after your infusion.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks to months before you and your doctor can tell if the medicine is working. Your doctor will check your progress through regular blood tests and scans throughout your treatment. Do not get discouraged if you do not feel better right away — the medicine is working inside your body even if you cannot feel it immediately.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): This medicine can be used in older adults, but side effects such as infections, nerve problems, and fatigue may be more pronounced. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver issues, as these may affect how your body handles the medicine and may require dose adjustments. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is NOT safe to use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. It can cause serious harm to an unborn baby or a nursing infant. Women of childbearing age must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Men must use birth control for at least 5 months after the last dose. This medicine may also affect fertility — talk to your doctor if this is a concern for you.
